newsitem.title: USA: National Semiconductor to acquire Cyrix.
newsitem.headline: National Semiconductor to acquire Cyrix.

text.p: National Semiconductor Corp. said Monday it agreed to buy Cyrix Corp. in a stock deal valued at $550 million.
The companies said in a joint news release that they plan to develop new computer chip technology for low-cost personal computer and information-appliance markets.

Cyrix shareholders would receive 0.825 of a National Semiconductor share for each Cyrix share held. National Semiconductor stock closed down 6.25 cents at $33.4375 in New York Stock Exchange trading, while Cyrix closed up $1.8125 to $23.0625 in Nasdaq trading, and was up another $2 in after-hours trading.

The tax-free transaction, which still must be approved by Cyrix shareholders, is expected to be completed in November 1997. National said it would take an unspecified, one-time charge in that quarter.

"Cyrix's family of high-performance and high-integration X86 processors will enable National Semiconductor to drive dramatic market growth for products such as network PCs, hand-held PCs, net browsers and other information appliances that are becoming extremely affordable," National Semiconductor Chief Executive Brian Halla said in a statement.
Earlier Monday, Intel Corp., National Semiconductor's Santa Clara, Calif., neighbour, said it would buy Chips & Technologies Inc. for $420 million in cash.
